_miab_broker_template.DELETE_THIS_KEY_BEFORE_USE: This block is documentation, not configuration. Remove it once you have merged what you need.
_miab_broker_template.what_this_is: The minimum openclaw.json shape that lets miab-broker + miab-observer work to full capacity. Merge these keys into your existing config -- do not replace your config with this file. Run `claw-callback.py doctor` afterwards to confirm.
_miab_broker_template.why_env_lives_here: Both skills read os.environ directly. The gateway is what launches agents, so a value exported in your shell is invisible to a wake fired by cron. skills.entries[].env is the only route that covers every path an agent can be started on.
_miab_broker_template.the_one_thing_people_get_wrong: The broker routes on the agents.entries key ('planner'). Agents self-identify by agents.entries[<id>].name ('SPECTRE'). (OpenClaw before 2026.9.3 used an agents.list[] array of {id, name}; doctor still reads that shape and warns.) The registry is keyed on id, so a return from SPECTRE misses it and the bottle strands. Declaring both here is not enough -- you must also register the persona as an alias. `doctor --commands-only` prints the exact calls.
required: tools.agentToAgent.enabled -- the transport dispatch_message rides. False looks like success: every command writes state and no wake is ever delivered.
skills.load.extraDirs must contain the directory holding the skill folders
_miab_broker_template.optional: Every other env var below has a working default. Set one only to move a specific file; setting them piecemeal is how the reader and writer end up on different ledgers.

bindings.comment: The origin agent needs at least one binding: it is where a human starts a task and where the resolved result lands. Its peer id is also what CLAW_CLOSED_TARGET is built from.
